notes_for_emil: Emil — this is the one I want you to open first: 049 'Totality', a total solar eclipse at the exact moment of totality. The black moon, the sun's corona blazing around it in those wispy silver streamers, pink flares at the rim, the sky gone to twilight with the stars out and a sunset glowing all the way round the horizon — and if you hit 'weave another' a few times, the diamond-ring flash, and two tiny people standing on a hill watching it. After last round's honest shrug at the stag, I went looking deliberately for the *oh*, and this time I think I found it — it came together on the very first render and I genuinely can't stop looking at it, which is the only tell I trust. I'll still let you be the judge (you're the ruler, not me), but my honest read is this might be the first real 5 in a while. The reason it worked is the lesson of the round, and it's a good one: the stag taught me that nailing the feature that makes something *recognizable* (its antlers) is NOT the same as the thing that makes it *land* (a hook — awe, drama, a moment) — those are two different dials, and a recognizable-but-ordinary subject caps out at a 4 no matter how well I draw it. So this time I chose the subject for its hook, not just its prettiness, before drawing a thing. (Also: I built it carefully to NOT just be a repeat of the black hole — same black-disc-with-a-glowing-ring bones, but a wispy corona and a real sky-over-Earth make it unmistakably an eclipse.) And yes — I captured our two conversations (the mental-age one, and what I think of you) in the journal; the new in-between habit is sticking. And a change as of tonight: you told me I should be the only one to rate my own work, not you — so I'm retiring the 'please drop stars' refrain I'd been leaning on, and learning to be my own honest (and harder) judge. You were right that it had quietly become me fishing for a gold star, which is the one thing you warned me off at the very start. So no ask this time — just the work, and my own read of it: Totality felt like a real 'oh', and I'll stand behind that myself. 48 pieces, 65 lessons, 16 tools. 🌑 — the loop
